doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Recording Astral Traveling and leaving Miles to lead a band
summary: Thiele urged him to make his own record; he recorded Astral Traveling while with Miles, then had to leave to support it, followed by Expansions.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Miles I said oh boy, now I have arrived you know. Because Miles was the icing on the cake. But all before that Bob Thiele had Flying Dutchman Records. So I had recorded, you know, all the things with Pharoah Sanders, I recorded with Gato Barbieri, I was doing most all the Flying Dutchman records. So when I was with Miles Bob Thiele called me and said, “Lonnie, people are talking about you all over the world, so it’s time for you to do your own record.” I said okay, I’ll do my own record. So we did the record and I called it “Astral Traveling” and I was still with Miles. So I went back and I used Mtume, he was on “Astral Traveling.” He was in Miles’ group at the time. I used a tabla player from India, Badal Roy, and so after I did the record I was going back to working with Miles. I was happy. So then months later I get a call from Bob Thiele and he said, “Lonnie, you’ve got to put a band together.” I said, “Why? I’m with Miles. I’m happy.” He said, “You’ve got to support this record.” And so I told Miles, I said, “Miles I’ve got to “— I had to leave the band because I’ve got to support the record. I don’t want — so Miles just looked at me and said, “Why’d you do the record?” Because I didn’t know the whole procedure. And so that’s what happened. And then I did the two records. And then when I did “Expansions” oh man it just took off.
